source.name: Progress on Water-related Ecosystems – 2024 Update
source.publisher: UN-Water and United Nations Environment Programme

cadence: Refresh with each UNEP and UN-Water SDG 6.6.1 progress assessment after reconciling observation epochs and basin definitions.
provenance: Reviewed global aggregated SDG 6.6.1 findings for freshwater ecosystem status, basin flow trends and exposed population. The freshwater species-population decline is retained as a report-cited global synthesis rather than a live taxon series.
uncertainty: Country reporting, satellite coverage, basin delineation, trend significance, observation epochs, monitoring density and national indicator composition vary. A country is counted degraded when at least one included ecosystem type is degraded; this does not mean every freshwater ecosystem in that country is degraded.
failure_behavior: Retain the last reviewed assessment and mark stale; reject changed country or basin denominators without reconciliation; never add potentially overlapping exposed populations, turn one degraded type into total national collapse, infer causes from flow change or fill unreported ecosystems with zero.

source_locators: UN-Water 2024 update: one or more water-related ecosystem types are degraded in 50 percent of countries, more than 90 of 185 reporting countries.
UN-Water 2024 report: freshwater species populations have declined globally by 83 percent since 1970.
UN-Water 2024 update: river flow significantly decreased in 402 of 12,572 basins, a fivefold increase from 15 years earlier, with 107.5 million people living in those basins.
UN-Water 2024 update: permanent surface water receded in 364 of 13,894 basins, where 93.1 million people live.

excluded_from_scoring: the sum of potentially overlapping reduced-flow and receding-water populations
unreported ecosystems treated as stable or degraded
